name: The Incarnation and Hypostatic Union

objectives.text: Identify from the Christmas account that God the Son was born as a real baby named Jesus to Mary
Name Jesus as both truly God and truly man
Retell the angel's announcements to Mary and to Joseph about the coming birth of Jesus
Describe from the Gospels ways Jesus showed a true human body and soul, such as growing, getting tired, being hungry, and weeping
Recite John 1:14 and explain in your own words what it means that the Word became flesh and dwelt among us
Explain the meaning of the name Immanuel and show how Matthew presents Jesus' birth as the fulfillment of Isaiah's prophecy
Explain the creed's confession that Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin Mary
Classify actions in a Gospel passage as showing Jesus' humanity or his deity, such as sleeping in the boat and calming the storm
Explain why Scripture teaches that the Son took a true body and a reasonable soul rather than only appearing to be human
Explain how Jesus shared fully in human nature yet was without sin
Analyze how the virgin conception by the Holy Spirit secures both Christ's true descent from Mary and the holiness of his human nature
Analyze the catechisms' reasons why the Mediator had to be true man, true God, and both in one person
Interpret the phrases form of God and form of a servant in Philippians 2 as describing the true deity and true humanity of the one Christ
Distinguish the theological terms person and nature as the church uses them to describe Christ
Explain the hypostatic union as the Reformed tradition confesses it, two whole and distinct natures joined in the one person of the eternal Son
Explain the church's teaching that the Son remains God and man in one person forever and did not lay aside his human nature
Trace the controversies over Christ's person raised by Apollinaris, Nestorius, and Eutyches that led to the Council of Chalcedon
Analyze the Chalcedonian Definition phrase by phrase, especially its confession of two natures without confusion, change, division, or separation
Evaluate Apollinarianism, Nestorianism, and Eutychianism against Scripture and the Chalcedonian Definition
Analyze Gospel texts that show Jesus' human knowledge and human will, such as his not knowing the hour and his prayer in Gethsemane, in light of two natures in one person
Defend the sinlessness and impeccability of Christ from Scripture and the doctrine of the hypostatic union
Explain the terms anhypostasia and enhypostasia and how they describe Christ's human nature as subsisting in the person of the Son
Analyze how Scripture ascribes the properties of either nature to the one person in the communicatio idiomatum
Compare the Reformed and Lutheran accounts of the communication of properties, including the Reformed teaching that the Son is not confined to his human nature

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (born of Mary, God and man, true humanity, John 1:14, Immanuel, classifying the natures, virgin conception, Philippians 2, why the Mediator is God and man, hypostatic union, Chalcedon, the heresies, sinlessness, communicatio idiomatum). Replaced the vague 'construct the Chalcedonian formula' with a phrase-by-phrase analysis and the vague 'compare without mixing' with a classification task. Added the creedal line on conception and birth, the need for a true body and soul, sinless humanity, the person and nature distinction, the permanence of the union, the historical controversies before Chalcedon, Christ's human knowledge and will, anhypostasia and enhypostasia, and the Reformed and Lutheran comparison. Corrected confession citations to numbered forms such as Westminster Confession of Faith 8.2 and 8.7, and added Heidelberg Q16-18 and Q47-48, WLC Q37 and Q40, WSC Q21-22, and Belgic Confession 18-19. Expanded the scripture citations to verse ranges. Left preexistence, kenosis as humiliation, offices, and atonement to the sibling sub-topics.
